name: KAAD Scholarship Programme 1 (Catholic Academic Exchange Service)
requiredDocuments: Online application form / questionnaire (kaad.de/en/scholarship-application; first stage)
Motivation letter (decisive for the personal-qualifications assessment)
Two recommendation letters from academic supervisors or other academics in your field

A reference from the country's Church (preferably the local bishop or a cleric) on your personal/religious convictions and Church/social engagement; candidates of other religions must be recommended by Catholic partners attesting commitment to interreligious dialogue (German or English translation)
Bachelor degree certificate (normally a four-year program or equivalent from an institution of recognised standing) with an above-average overall grade
Acceptance/admission letter from the German university where you intend to study
Proof of German language proficiency (Goethe B2 level for German-taught programs; basic German before starting for English-taught programs)

timeline.deadline: January 15 and June 30 (two rounds per year; applications must be received in Bonn by these dates)
timeline.resultsBy: Decisions in March and September; all candidates contacted personally by email within about three months of the deadline
timeline.notes: KAAD runs two fixed application rounds every year (received in Bonn by 15 January and 30 June; selection in March and September). Per the official KAAD Asia department S1 guidance these are recurring annual dates; documented here for the 2025-2026 cycle (anchor 2026-06). Partner committees may impose earlier internal cut-offs, since applications are routed through them first.

benefits: Covers study and living costs (KAAD: scholarships 'cover study and living costs comparable to those of other exchange organizations'; financed by German Catholic church taxes, diocesan funds, German government ministries and donors)
One-year study grant for a master's degree at a German university, renewable yearly up to a maximum of 3 years

4-6 months of German language and culture training in Bonn at the start of the stay (for English-taught programs); language/culture training of four to six months also possible for German-taught programs
Personal, spiritual and academic support plus access to KAAD's worldwide scholar/alumni network and accompanying educational program/seminars
mustKnow: Return-home bond: KAAD expects holders to return to their home country after studying in Germany — otherwise the scholarship is converted into a loan.

Routed via a Catholic partner committee: you apply online to KAAD Bonn first; after a positive initial evaluation your application is forwarded to the local partner committee (in Bangladesh: Caritas Bangladesh, Dhaka) — it is a two-step process and partner committees may set earlier internal deadlines.

Faith preference: most grant holders are Catholic (a few candidates of no or other religious affiliation are selected each year); applicants of another religion (e.g. Muslims) can be funded only if proposed/recommended by Catholic partners and showing a documentable willingness to engage in interreligious dialogue.
Theology students and theologians are NOT funded; all other disciplines are welcome.

German language is required even for English-taught programs (at least A2 German for the compulsory educational program for English-taught tracks, B1 generally; B2 Goethe level expected at the time of application for German-taught programs).
Two academic recommendation letters plus a Church reference (bishop/cleric) are mandatory parts of the application.
A university acceptance/admission letter is required as part of the application.
Bangladesh is one of KAAD's six Asia focus countries; applications from non-focus countries are 'only considered in exceptional cases'.
No fixed monthly stipend figure is published on KAAD's public pages — confirm the exact amount with KAAD / the partner committee.

universities: Any recognised German university (applicant must secure admission/acceptance)

duration: 1 year, renewable yearly up to a maximum of 3 years (master's/doctoral)
eligibleNationalities: Nationals of and residents in developing/emerging countries in Africa, Asia, the Middle East and Latin America; for Asia, KAAD concentrates on six focus countries — Bangladesh, Indonesia, Myanmar, Philippines, Vietnam, and PR China. Bangladeshi nationals are eligible.
languageRequirements: German-taught programs: German at Goethe B2 level at the time of application. English-taught programs: at least A2 German for the compulsory educational program, with basic German before starting; scholarship includes 4-6 months language/culture training in Bonn. No IELTS/TOEFL requirement stated by KAAD.
bondObligation: Must return to home country after studies; failure to return converts the scholarship into a loan
renewalConditions: Annual renewal up to a maximum of 3 years; continued satisfactory study progress and participation in KAAD's compulsory accompanying educational program
postStudyWork: Program is explicitly reintegration-oriented (return home expected); not a stay-back scheme
